newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: FOCUS-Manila stocks seen climbing steadily.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Manila stocks seen climbing steadily.

text.p: Philippine shares chalked up their fourth straight of gains on Tuesday, in their second biggest jump of the year, and analysts said the market's recent woes may finally be behind it.

"It was one of the best days ever in the market. The way we see it, negative sentiment which has largely weighed down the market has improved. This is a good beginning for a reversal," said Helen Alvarez, research director at All Asia Capital.

On Tuesday, the main index shot up 4.34 percent to a close of 2,710.91. The market barometer's biggest rise was last May 5 when it closed with a 131-point gain due to demand for underpriced blue chips.
Traders said that though Tuesday's turnover at 2.08 billion pesos was still lower than the daily average, it has been improving in recent days.

Diversified Securities executive vice-president Jose Ricardo Garcia said that although thirdliners were the focus early in the session, foreign investors were later seen moving into firstliner issues such as Ayala Land Inc and Manila Electric Co B propping up the main index in late trade.

"The market has been showing some strength since last week and today's gains may be a sign that the market is recovering due to macroeconomic news. We have started to adopt a back-to-the-basics strategy and are recommending a buy on big cap issues," said Kenneth Nerecina, research head at Vickers Ballas Securities Phils Inc.

Analysts traced the market's recent climb to last week's U.S. decision leaving interest rates unchanged followed by release of improved first quarter growth in the domestic agricultural sector and a successful speech by President Fidel Ramos at an investors' forum in Hong Kong last week.
The Philippine stock market has been reeling largely from fears of a property crash and a financial scare similar to Thailand.
From its all-time high of 3,447.60 points in February, the main index fell nearly 28 percent when it reached its lowest close for the year at 2,499.38 points last week.
"At this point, any correction will not be lower than 2,500. With good GNP (gross national product) results, we are on our way to a reversal," said Bing Trinidad, sales manager at DBS Securities.
First quarter GNP figure is set to be released later this week.
All Asia's Alvarez added market may experience a brief pullback due to Tuesday's sharp rise but will resume a gradual climb with resistance at 2,800 points.
"The worst is over. People are more confident and are slowly re-entering the market," said Noel Reyes, research head at Anscor-Hagedorn Securities.
